full_caption: Evanthe Thackeray-Bell, Appellant, v. Larkspur Hill Capital Servicing, LLC, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: This appeal concerns a claimed easement of access across the northern 40 feet of the parcel at 3254 Pennyroyal Court, Rooksbury, FH, owned by Larkspur Hill Capital Servicing, LLC, in favor of the landlocked rear parcel owned by Evanthe Thackeray-Bell.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: An easement by necessity arises where (1) the dominant and servient estates were formerly held in common ownership, (2) that unity was severed, and (3) the necessity for the way existed at the moment of severance. Necessity arising afterward will not support the easement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: An easement by prescription requires use that is open, notorious, continuous, hostile and under a claim of right for the full statutory period of 20 years. Permissive use, however long continued, never ripens into a prescriptive right.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The evidence showed that Evanthe Thackeray-Bell and predecessors drove a gravel track across the servient estate from 2002 through 2014, maintained it with periodic grading, and installed a culvert at the drainage swale in 2020.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The scope of an easement is fixed by the use that created it. A prescriptive way established by passenger vehicles and light farm equipment does not expand to accommodate commercial haul traffic of the character now proposed by Evanthe Thackeray-Bell.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The common grantor conveyed the rear parcel in 2002 without any reservation of a right of way. At that time the rear parcel abutted the abandoned rail grade, which was subsequently vacated by the Rooksbury County Board, leaving the parcel without lawful access.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Because the want of access arose from the later vacation of a public road rather than from the severance itself, no easement by necessity was created. The trial court's contrary conclusion was error.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The servient owner retains the right to make any use of the burdened land that does not unreasonably interfere with the easement. Installation of a gate is permissible provided it is not locked against the dominant owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: An easement appurtenant runs with the land and passes on conveyance of the dominant estate whether or not it is mentioned in the deed. It is extinguished only by release, merger, abandonment, or prescription running against it.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The judgment declaring a prescriptive easement is affirmed as to the way as historically used, and modified to exclude the proposed commercial expansion. Costs to Larkspur Hill Capital Servicing, LLC.

sections.heading: RIDER 4 — RELOCATION
sections.text: Grantor may relocate the easement at Grantor's sole cost upon 30 days' written notice, provided the relocated way is of equal width and grade, provides equal utility and access, and does not increase the distance of travel by more than 3 percent. Grantee's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

sections.heading: RIDER 5 — TERMINATION AND NON-ABANDONMENT
sections.text: This easement terminates only by written release recorded in the land records, by merger of the dominant and servient estates in a single owner, or by a court decree. Non-use, however long continued, shall not constitute abandonment absent a recorded release or an affirmative act by Grantee manifesting an intent permanently to relinquish the right.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Fairhollow.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Waiver and Course of Dealing
sections.text: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party charged. The acceptance of a payment with knowledge of a breach, the failure to insist on strict performance, or any course of dealing between the parties shall not constitute a waiver of that or any subsequent breach, nor estop the party from enforcing the provision thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Notice
sections.text: Every notice required or permitted shall be in writing and shall be deemed given: on personal delivery; on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, certified, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier. Notices to a party shall be sent to the address last furnished by that party in writing. Electronic mail alone does not constitute notice unless the recipient acknowledges receipt in writing.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.
